title: Liquidity-withdrawal reversal: fade a large one-hour move only when the quoted spread widened during it (quotes withdrawn), with a no-spread-condition control and a scheduled-news control at stage A, on USDJPY first
rationale: Mechanism (Nagel 2012, 'Evaporating liquidity'; Brunnermeier and Pedersen 2009; Mancini, Ranaldo and Wrampelmeyer 2013 for FX): short-term price reversals are the compensation liquidity providers earn for absorbing order imbalances, and that compensation is large only when liquidity supply is scarce. In FX the scarcity is observable: when dealers and ECN liquidity providers pull or widen their quotes, the top-of-book spread widens against its normal level at that time of day. A large move that happens while quotes are withdrawn is, in part, a price concession paid by an impatient liquidity demander (a stop cascade, a forced hedger, a margin-driven seller) to the few providers still quoting; once quoting resumes, the concession is competed away and the price retraces. The same-sized move made with normal, tight quotes is information being priced by a deep book and should not retrace; this is what every prior fade in this programme measured, and they all lost (session reversal, Asian-extreme fade, quiet-hours Bollinger fade -0.062 R, sweep fades, one-day shock fade -0.10 R on EURUSD; and after 3292 USDJPY box stop-outs the price kept going the stop way, +0.08 R at 30 minutes and +0.11 R at one hour, gj-strat after_sl). Those tests conditioned on clock, level or size, never on the state of liquidity supply, so their negatives are consistent with this hypothesis rather than against it, and any edge here must come from the spread condition alone; the tick-volume test (fx_volume_climax_reversal) tried to measure liquidity demand with a quantity that does not measure it, and its lesson forbids volume, not spread. The quoted spread is the one data dimension in this store that no prior test has used as a signal input (its only earlier appearance is the entry spread as one feature inside the box_meta logistic filter). What the arm measures in practice (the Critic's counts, design years, no outcomes): the typical qualifying episode is a one-hour mid-price move of at least 0.25 x ATR20 (median 40 pips on USDJPY) during which the bar's quoted-spread proxy widens from a slot median of about 0.5 pips to about 1.3 pips (median ratio 2.25), outside the scheduled-announcement blocks; in 70 percent of flagged bars an M1 open or close quote inside the bar was at least twice the norm, so the proxy mostly reflects real quotes. It is an operational definition of mild, frequent quote withdrawal in fast markets, not of dealers leaving the market; the famous episodes are mostly not in the tested arm (2011-03-17 and 2013-05-23 contribute nothing, 2010-05-06 one bar at 23:30 UTC, 2015-08-24 four episodes, 2016-06-24 three). Design: bars M15 on USDJPY (0.6 pip median spread; the classic liquidity-gap currency). The state is the bar's spread proxy relative to the median of the same 15-minute slot over its previous 20 occurrences, so the daily spread profile cancels out; the rollover window [20:45, 22:15) UTC is always excluded because its asymmetric widening distorts the mid price. Two controls sit in the stage A grid: spread_ratio_min = 0 (no spread condition; the plain intraday shock fade, which the mechanism and the prior evidence say is about zero or negative) and exclude_news = false (keeps moves inside the scheduled-release blocks; these are information-driven and the mechanism predicts no reversal there, which the NFP fade result of -0.12 R already suggests). The hypothesis arm is spread_ratio_min 2 with exclude_news true at move_atr_min 0.25; the controls run only at stage A, and stages B, C, the walk-forward and any holdout run the hypothesis arm alone, because the pipeline ranks cells by design t and a 2,000-trade control would otherwise outrank a 135-trade hypothesis cell. Sample: USDJPY has 160 design episodes on 123 distinct trading days at move_atr_min 0.25 (83 at 0.40, a stage A surface point only; the earlier 135-on-105 count came from a float comparison that dropped exact-tie bars and was corrected at code review before any run); a few dates hold many of them (2015-08-24/25, the 2016 US election night, Brexit, a BoJ day), so t is also reported date-clustered. Stage B uses each market's own release blocks as well as the US ones, which leaves EURUSD 64, GBPUSD 35, AUDUSD 24, EURJPY 41, GBPJPY 37, AUDJPY 17 and XAUUSD 82 design episodes: a thin replication of about 300 episodes over seven markets, read pooled and date-clustered rather than market by market. Costs: the spread at the fill averages 0.90 pips at entry_delay_bars 0 and 0.83 at delay 1, so the round trip is about 1.8-1.9 pips (half the spread each way, 0.4 pip of slippage, about 0.7 pip of commission), about 0.05 R on the median 40-pip move, about 0.08 R at the p10 move and about 0.10 R at 2x costs; 0.04-0.08 R on the stage B markets (GBPJPY and AUDJPY fills average 5.9 and 4.5 pips after a flag). The entry_delay_bars = 1 arm is a latency and timing check (how fast the reversion happens and what 15 minutes of execution delay costs), not a cheaper fill. Expected: a net +0.08 R needs a gross of about +0.13 R, a mean retracement of about 13 percent of the move within two hours; with 160 episodes and sd 0.6-0.7 R the expected design t is 1.3-1.6 trade-level and lower date-clustered, so stage A has only about a 60 percent chance of passing even if the effect is real: a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence. Live execution caveat, stated up front: the trigger is defined on Dukascopy's quote feed, a prop-firm feed widens on its own schedule, so live signals must be computed from a Dukascopy feed and executed on the prop account; the setup fires about 17 times a year at unpredictable hours (44 percent between 23:00 and 03:00 UTC), so it needs an EA rather than a screen; and the executor's intrabar stop fill at the level plus 0.2 pip is optimistic in exactly these thin markets (expected bias small, about 0.01-0.02 R with a 40-pip stop, but with a fat tail), which the stop-exit gap report in stage C is there to show.
rules:
All times UTC. Bars: M15, labelled by open time; a bar's close time is ts + 15 minutes. Bars are sparse; locate by timestamp and never assume one bar per slot.

DEFINITIONS (all computed from closed bars 0..i):
- mid_c[i] = (bid_c[i] + ask_c[i]) / 2. The one-hour move ending at bar i is move[i] = mid_c[i] - mid_c[i-4]; valid only if i >= 4 and ts[i] - ts[i-4] <= max_gap_min (75) minutes, otherwise no signal at i.
- ATR20[i] = F.atr_prev(F.daily_bars(m), 20) mapped to bars with daily.to_bars (known at the start of the trading day); must be finite and > 0.
- Quoted-spread proxy of bar i: spr[i] = max(ask_o[i] - bid_o[i], ask_c[i] - bid_c[i], ask_h[i] - bid_h[i], ask_l[i] - bid_l[i]) in price units (the loader clamps ask >= bid).
- Slot norm: slot[i] = F.minute_of_day_utc(m)[i]. norm[i] = median of spr over the previous norm_window (20) bars that share slot[i], strictly before bar i. Loop over the 96 slots, never over bars: for a slot with ascending bar indices idx, norm[idx[k]] = median(spr[idx[k-W:k]]) for k >= W (numpy sliding_window_view over the slot's spr values, median over axis 1, window r assigned to idx[r + W]) and NaN otherwise. ratio[i] = spr[i] / norm[i], used only where norm is finite and > 0. Every arm, including the control, requires norm to be defined, so all arms cover the same period.
- Move window of bar i: [ts[i] + 15 min - 60 min, ts[i] + 15 min). With mod = the open minute-of-day of bar i: ws = (mod - 45) mod 1440 and we = (mod + 15) mod 1440. For a block [b0, b1) in minutes of day: if ws < we, the window overlaps the block when ws < b1 and b0 < we; if ws >= we, the window crosses 00:00 UTC (this includes we == 0) and overlaps when ws < b1 or b0 < we.
- ROLLOVER block, always applied in every arm (a data-quality exclusion, not news: the asymmetric rollover widening distorts the mid price): [20:45, 22:15) = minutes [1245, 1335).
- NEWS blocks, applied only when exclude_news is true: US blocks [12:00, 15:30) and [18:00, 20:00) = minutes [720, 930) and [1080, 1200) on every market, plus the blocks of each leg of m.sym (letters 0-2 and 3-5): JPY [03:00, 05:00) = [180, 300); EUR [06:00, 10:15) and [11:30, 12:00) = [360, 615) and [690, 720); GBP [06:00, 10:15) and [10:45, 12:00) = [360, 615) and [645, 720); AUD [00:15, 02:15) and [03:00, 05:00) = [15, 135) and [180, 300); USD and XAU have no blocks of their own. USDJPY therefore keeps exactly its four registered blocks: [03:00, 05:00), [12:00, 15:30), [18:00, 20:00) and the rollover.

CANDIDATE BAR i: valid move, valid ATR20 and norm; |move[i]| >= move_atr_min * ATR20[i]; ratio[i] >= spread_ratio_min evaluated tie-safe as ratio[i] >= spread_ratio_min * (1 - 1e-9), because spreads are quantised at 0.1 pip so a true ratio is 2a/b for integers a and b and an exact tie must count as >= (spread_ratio_min = 0 is the no-spread-condition control arm and is satisfied wherever norm is defined); the move window does not overlap the rollover block; and (exclude_news is false OR the move window overlaps no NEWS block).

EPISODES (one trade per episode): loop over the candidate indices only, in ascending order. Accept i if i >= last + cooldown_bars (12, three hours) and set last = i at acceptance, BEFORE any delay check, so both entry_delay_bars arms use the same episode set.

ORDER PLACEMENT: j = i + entry_delay_bars (0 or 1). Skip the episode if j >= m.n, or if entry_delay_bars > 0 and ts[j] - ts[i] > delay_max_gap_min (30) minutes. All signal fields are written at index j and use only information from bars <= j; never read ts[j+1] or any field of the fill bar.
- If move[i] > 0: entry_short[j] = True (fade an up move). If move[i] < 0: entry_long[j] = True (fade a down move).
- entry_type[j] = 0 (market at the open of bar j + 1: ask for longs, bid for shorts), valid_bars[j] = 1.
- sl_dist[j] = stop_mult (1.0) * |move[i]|, so 1 R = the size of the move being faded; always > 0 because |move[i]| >= move_atr_min * ATR20 > 0.
- tp_dist[j] = NaN (no target; the time exit measures the mean retracement).
- max_bars[j] = hold_bars (8, about two hours). No exit_long / exit_short signals, no other filters, no pyramiding (the executor blocks entries while a position is open).

PARAMETERS, every one read from p: spread_ratio_min (grid 0, 2), move_atr_min (grid 0.25, 0.40), exclude_news (grid true, false), entry_delay_bars (grid 0, 1); fixed: stop_mult 1.0, hold_bars 8, cooldown_bars 12, norm_window 20, max_gap_min 75, delay_max_gap_min 30.

GRIDS: stage A on USDJPY runs the 16-cell grid above; it is the only place the control arms run. Stages B and C, the walk-forward and any holdout run only the hypothesis arm: spread_ratio_min 2, exclude_news true, move_atr_min 0.25, entry_delay_bars 0 and 1 (2 cells). The Director sets stage_a.grid (16 cells) and grid (2 cells) in specs/auto/fx_liquidity_withdrawal_reversal.json after the review step and before the test; the module GRID stays at the 16 cells so the checker exercises every value.

SANITY COUNTS (signal bars on USDJPY M15, 2010-2017 only, counted by the Critic before any run with these exact definitions): defaults 160 at both delays; spread_ratio_min 0 2,075; exclude_news false (rollover still excluded) 567; move_atr_min 0.4 83 (271 with news included); EURUSD defaults 64 with the EUR blocks, GBPUSD 35, AUDUSD 24, EURJPY 41, GBPJPY 37, AUDJPY 17, XAUUSD 82. These are the counts after the tie-safe threshold comparison (ratio >= threshold * (1 - 1e-9)); the earlier figures (135 / 522 / 76 / 57) came from a float comparison that dropped 37 of the 106 exact-tie bars on USDJPY and were corrected at code review, before any run. A count that differs by more than about 10 percent means the window-overlap or slot-median logic is wrong and must be fixed before anything else.

REPORTING (computed from the trades; stage A table and stage C): per arm the number of episodes, avg R, trade-level t and date-clustered t (R averaged per 17:00 New York trading day), the mean quoted spread at the fill bar's open in pips, gross R before spread and commission, and design years individually. Stage C additions: (a) the share of trades that exit at the stop and the mean of (mae_r - 1) on those exits, to show gap exposure; (b) avg R without the 5 trading days with the largest total R (a diagnostic, not a gate: removing the best 5 of about 123 days costs about 0.05-0.07 R by construction even if the effect is real); (c) episodes whose move window contains the 23:50 UTC Japan releases or the 06:30 UTC BoJ press conference, reported separately; (d) episodes whose move window contains 16:00 UTC in UK winter (the WM/R fix) or 00:55 UTC on a gotobi day, reported separately and removed for the fix-flow kill rule; (e) design, check and walk-forward statistics pooled over the seven non-primary markets, date-clustered across markets.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Hypothesis-cell floor on USDJPY, applied by the Director even if the pipeline reports a candidate (the automatic stage A gate ranks all 16 cells by t, and a 2,000-trade control can outrank a 160-trade hypothesis cell): the hypothesis cell (spread_ratio_min 2, exclude_news true, move_atr_min 0.25, at whichever entry_delay_bars has the higher design t) must have design avg R > 0, trade-level t >= 1 and date-clustered t >= 1 (R averaged per 17:00 New York trading day), with at least 120 episodes; otherwise scrap. (2) Control: at the same move_atr_min and entry_delay_bars with exclude_news true, avg R(spread_ratio_min 2) minus avg R(spread_ratio_min 0) must be >= +0.08 R in design; if the plain intraday shock fade earns as much, the spread adds nothing and the hypothesis dies. (3) Information control: at spread_ratio_min 2 with the rollover excluded in both, the news-inclusive arm (exclude_news false) must not beat the non-news arm by more than 0.05 R in design; if moves inside the scheduled blocks revert more, the effect is overreaction to news, not liquidity provision, and the liquidity label is scrapped with that lesson. (4) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands and the mean fill spread per arm is reported; if the delay 0 arm is positive gross but negative net and the delay 1 arm is also negative, the lesson is that the concession is real but belongs to the liquidity providers already quoting, not to a market-order taker. (5) Regime: at least half of the design years positive at the chosen cell. (6) Fix flow: design avg R at the chosen cell must stay > 0 after removing the episodes whose move window contains 16:00 UTC in UK winter (the WM/R fix) or 00:55 UTC on a gotobi day; if it does not, the effect is fix flow, which has already been measured (prior_fix_fades, gotobi short), and the hypothesis is dead. (7) Replication: at the hypothesis cell, design avg R pooled over the seven non-primary markets (EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, EURJPY, GBPJPY, AUDJPY, XAUUSD, each with its own release blocks) must be > 0, with its date-clustered t reported; the pooled-check hard gate (avg R > 0 with >= 30 trades) and the walk-forward gate stand, and the pooled check and walk-forward statistics are also reported date-clustered across markets. AUDUSD (24 design episodes) and AUDJPY (17) fall under the pipeline's 30-trade floor and enter only the pooled replication. Honest expectations: USDJPY design has 160 episodes on 123 trading days at move_atr_min 0.25 (the 0.40 cells, 83 episodes, are a stage A surface point only; counts corrected at code review for the tie-safe comparison, before any run); all-in cost about 0.05 R (fill spread 0.90 pips at delay 0, 0.83 at delay 1, median move 40 pips) and about 0.10 R at 2x costs; a net +0.08 R needs a gross of about +0.13 R, a mean retracement of about 13 percent of the move; expected design t 1.3-1.6 trade-level, lower date-clustered. If the true effect is +0.08 R, a stage A kill has roughly a 30-35 percent chance of being a false negative, so a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence.

why_different: Every prior fade in the index conditioned on the clock (session reversal, Tokyo-open contrarian, quiet-hours Bollinger fade, night scalp), on a price level (sweeps of the previous session's extreme, round numbers, Asian-range fade), on the size of a one-day move (shock fade, z-score fade) or on tick volume (volume climax); none conditioned on the state of liquidity supply, and none used the quoted spread as a signal (its only earlier appearance is as one feature in the box_meta logistic filter). This hypothesis uses the spread as the state variable, works at the intraday episode horizon (one-hour moves on M15 bars with a two-hour hold) rather than the session or the day, and carries its own falsification structure at stage A: a no-spread-condition arm (spread_ratio_min 0) that reproduces the known negative baseline inside the same design, and a scheduled-news arm that the mechanism predicts to be worse. The tick-volume lesson forbids volume as an input and the follow-the-shock mirror; neither is used here. The NFP fade (edge_hunt) faded a single scheduled release at a fixed clock time, which is exactly the information-driven case this design puts in the control arm.
